observations: The page number «20» stands at the head of the page, centred, with a rule below it. L01-L02: the heading of chapter 26, in bold, centred, in two lines; in the left margin beside it «C 75r, O 132v». L23: the heading of chapter 27, in bold, centred, without a folio beside it.

L06-L22: the oblique ascensions from the noon shadow at the equinox of a gnomon of twelve digits: the shadow times 114, divided by 115, is the argument of Aries; the shadow times 113, divided by 116, that of Taurus; a third of the shadow that of Gemini. Each argument is subtracted from the right ascension of its sign for the sign and its opposite companion, and added for the other pair. L13: «race elhamel», the head of the Ram (raʾs al-ḥamal), the first point of Aries; L16 «bilmustakim», in the right sphere (bi-l-mustaqīm), in italics.

Checked against the ascensional differences for the obliquity of 23° 51′ (p. 19, L07-L08): the difference grows by about 0.986 degree per digit of the shadow over Aries, 0.799 over Taurus and 0.326 over Gemini; the rule for Aries (114/115 = 0.991) and the rule for Gemini (1/3) agree with these to about one and two in a hundred, the rule for Taurus (113/116 = 0.974) does not; 113/141 would give 0.801. To be compared with Suter's commentary on the chapter (p. 73).

N02 and N08: «elhaazem (?)» and «indicavit (?)», the bracket 10 and 8 px from the word, a thin space. N01-N02: the four words that O writes above the heading of chapter 26 are those that Suter discusses on p. XXII (JP2 0026, L09-L16).
The colons and semicolons of the text stand after the thin space of the edition (10-12 px measured).

critical_notes.evidence: the sentence on Aries ends with «indicat», and the rule for Taurus begins with a capital, «Item ad taurum», as «designabit{sup:23}). Item ad geminos.» (L17-L18); a comma is printed where the full stop is needed
